data.title: How Investors May Respond To Clorox (CLX) Thin Dividend Coverage
data.description:
• Clorox reported that shareholders at its November 18, 2026 virtual annual meeting ratified Ernst & Young LLP as independent auditor and the board declared a US$1.25 quarterly dividend payable on February 12, 2027 to holders of record on January 27, 2027.
  • The declared payout comes as Clorox's dividend has recently exceeded free cash flow at about 133%, which points to pressure on cash generation while a new CEO prepares to take charge in January 2027.
  • The focus now turns to how Clorox's stretched dividend coverage shapes the broader investment narrative and what that might mean for investors.

Clorox Investment Narrative Recap

To own Clorox, you effectively need to believe the health and hygiene focus, ERP optimization and GOJO integration described in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St can support steady earnings while consumers keep trading down and shopping club and mass channels. The biggest near term swing factor remains how quickly productivity and mix help margins cope with over US$200 million of forecast cost inflation.

The key risk right now is cash generation. Dividend payouts are running at about 133% of free cash flow and roughly 85% to 90% of net earnings, which tightens room to invest while servicing debt that is not well covered by operating cash flow. If margin rebuilding stalls, capital allocation options narrow.

The US$1.25 quarterly dividend affirmation is the clearest touchpoint for that cash flow story. It keeps roughly US$600 million of annual dividend commitments in place even as free cash flow coverage remains thin and supply chain and input costs are guided to be significantly above historical levels in fiscal 2027.

For you as an income focused holder, this payout decision keeps the dividend stream intact for now but also concentrates attention on execution under the incoming CEO from January 2027. Progress on ERP benefits, GOJO and broader productivity will be watched closely because they underpin both dividend sustainability and any room to reduce leverage over the next few years.

Clorox's current analyst storyline implies revenues of US$8.1b and earnings of US$789.0 million by 2029, based on forecast revenue growth of 6.3% a year and an earnings increase of about US$202.0 million from US$587.0 million today.

data.title: Can 3M (MMM) Trade At A Discount After UBS Growth Call?
data.description:
3M has delivered a very strong 138.2% share price gain over the past three years, which puts a bright spotlight on one thing: whether the current US$177.99 price can be backed up by the cash the business is expected to generate. With upbeat commentary around its earnings potential running well into the next decade, investors are increasingly asking how that story lines up with an intrinsic value grounded in hard cash flows rather than sentiment.

  • The 138.2% return over three years means anyone looking at 3M today is effectively being asked to pay a much higher price for the same underlying cash flow stream than they were a few years ago, so the link between that stream and the share price matters more than ever.
  • UBS now expects stronger earnings and margin expansion helped by productivity gains, pricing and a shift toward more customer-focused product development, which can support higher and more durable cash generation if execution matches those expectations.
  • If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why 3M's 26.0x P/E tells a different valuation story.

The issue now is whether 3M's current share price lines up with its intrinsic value when that value is estimated using a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view of the cash the company can return over time.

If you are weighing whether 3M's 138.2% three year return is justified by its cash flows, it can help to compare that story with companies in the 40 high quality undervalued stocks.

Does 3M Look Undervalued on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) view here focuses on the cash that 3M can realistically return to shareholders over time. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $2.6b, with the model assuming that this stream progresses into a growing profile over the next decade rather than shrinking.

Those projections build toward annual free cash flow in the mid 4b to mid 5b range by 2030, which is then discounted back using the 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity approach. The outcome is an estimated intrinsic value that the model suggests is meaningfully above the current US$177.99 share price. Because UBS is highlighting potential earnings and margin gains through 2030, the outlook on profitability helps explain why the cash flow based value comes out higher than where the market is pricing 3M today. data.title: Insider Buyers Lose Additional kr754k As Elliptic Laboratories Dips To kr297m
data.description:
The recent 18% drop in Elliptic Laboratories ASA's (OB:ELABS) stock could come as a blow to insiders who purchased kr4.30m worth of stock at an average buy price of kr2.85 over the past 12 months. Insiders buy with the expectation to see their investments rise in value over a period of time. However, recent losses have rendered their above investment worth kr3.55m which is not ideal.

While we would never suggest that investors should base their decisions solely on what the directors of a company have been doing, we do think it is perfectly logical to keep tabs on what insiders are doing.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Elliptic Laboratories Insider Transactions Over The Last Year

Over the last year, we can see that the biggest insider purchase was by insider Edvin Austbo for kr4.2m worth of shares, at about kr2.85 per share. So it's clear an insider wanted to buy, even at a higher price than the current share price (being kr2.35). Their view may have changed since then, but at least it shows they felt optimistic at the time. We always take careful note of the price insiders pay when purchasing shares. As a general rule, we feel more positive about a stock if insiders have bought shares at above current prices, because that suggests they viewed the stock as good value, even at a higher price.

Elliptic Laboratories insiders may have bought shares in the last year, but they didn't sell any. You can see the insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year depicted in the chart below. Elliptic Laboratories is not the only stock that insiders are buying. For those who like to find small cap companies at attractive valuations, this free list of growing companies with recent insider purchasing, could be just the ticket.

Insider Ownership

I like to look at how many shares insiders own in a company, to help inform my view of how aligned they are with insiders. A high insider ownership often makes company leadership more mindful of shareholder interests. Insiders own 20% of Elliptic Laboratories shares, worth about kr59m. This level of insider ownership is good but just short of being particularly stand-out. It certainly does suggest a reasonable degree of alignment.

So What Do The Elliptic Laboratories Insider Transactions Indicate?

The fact that there have been no Elliptic Laboratories insider transactions recently certainly doesn't bother us. However, our analysis of transactions over the last year is heartening. Overall we don't see anything to make us think Elliptic Laboratories insiders are doubting the company, and they do own shares.
